question.text: Ms. Deepika Rao's Cat I VCF is researching a Series A candidate. Chapter 9 lists three market-size metrics VC investors use. Which triplet correctly defines them in descending order?

answer.text: TAM > SAM > SOM: Total Addressable Market → Serviceable Available Market → Serviceable Obtainable Market.
SAM > TAM > SOM: Serviceable Available Market is the widest universe.
SOM > SAM > TAM: Serviceable Obtainable is always the biggest.
TAM = SAM = SOM: the three are synonymous in the Chapter 9 framework.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 defines TAM as the full market size, SAM as 'how much TAM can be realistically achieved … based on its business model', and SOM as the 'percentage of the SAM that can be captured in the long run'. So TAM (widest) > SAM > SOM (narrowest). The Trap: Options B and C invert the nested relationship. Option D treats the three metrics as identical, which defeats the layered TAM/SAM/SOM construction the workbook describes. Note: The TAM > SAM > SOM ordering is taken directly from page 207 of the workbook; no additional valuation rule-of-thumb is layered on.
